title: Digraphs sh/ch/th/ng
examples: Can you show me the 'sh' sound?
How do I know when to use 'th'?

explain.say: Listen carefully. Two letters can make one sound. This is called a digraph. Say 'sh' like in the word ship.
Next, let us hear the 'ch' sound. Say 'ch' like in the word chip. Remember to keep your mouth open a little.
Now for 'th'. Try to put your tongue between your teeth. Say 'th' like in the word thin. This sound is tricky.
The 'ng' sound is at the end of words. Say 'ng' like in the word sing. It sounds like humming.
Look at the word ship. Can you see the 'sh' at the start? That is a digraph making one sound.

faq.a: A digraph is when two letters work together to make one single sound. It is like two friends making one noise together.
asks: Are two letters always one sound?

faq.q: How do I know which sound to use?
faq.a: Sometimes you just have to listen carefully to the word. If you hear the sound, look for the two letters that make it.
asks: Should I just guess the sound?
Is there a rule for when to use 'sh'?

faq.a: Yes, 'ck' makes a short /k/ sound at the end of a word. For example, in the word back.
The letters 'qu' often make the /kw/ sound, like in the word queen. You usually see them together.

faq.q: How do I spot a digraph in a word?
faq.a: You look for two letters right next to each other that make a sound you know. Try sounding out the word slowly.
asks: How do I circle the digraph?

facts: A digraph is two letters that make one sound.
Common digraphs include sh, ch, th, and ng.
The letters 'ck' make a short /k/ sound at the end of words.
'Qu' often makes the /kw/ sound in words.

quiz.say: Which pair of letters makes the sound /sh/?
quiz.why: The letters 's' and 'h' together make the /sh/ sound.

wrong.1: This is only one letter, so it cannot be a digraph.
wrong.2: The letters 'c' and 'h' make a different sound, /ch/.
wrong.3: The letters must touch each other to make the sound.

quiz.say: In the word 'chip', which letters make the /ch/ sound?
quiz.why: The letters 'c' and 'h' are together and make the /ch/ sound.

wrong.0: These letters are separated and do not make the sound.
wrong.1: You are using too many letters to make the sound.
wrong.3: This only uses one letter, so it is not a digraph.

quiz.say: Which pair of letters makes the sound /ng/ at the end?
quiz.why: The letters 'n' and 'g' together make the /ng/ sound, like in sing.

wrong.0: The letters must be touching to make the sound.
wrong.2: This is only one letter, so it cannot be a digraph.
wrong.3: This is also only one letter, not a digraph.
